$comment: Advisories consciously accepted, with an expiry date that forces re-review.
This is NOT a way to silence the audit gate: scripts/audit-gate.mjs fails the
build for any advisory that is not listed here, and ALSO fails for any entry
whose reviewBy date has passed. Adding an entry requires a real applicability

allow.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
justification: NOT REACHABLE IN THIS APPLICATION. The attack is a brace pattern nested deep
enough to exhaust the stack, and it needs an attacker to choose the pattern.
Here braces runs only at build time, inside Tailwind CSS 3: its content
scanner (micromatch) and file watcher (chokidar) expand the two globs in
written in the repository, with one level of braces. No app code or script
imports braces, micromatch, chokidar or fast-glob, and none of them is in the
built bundle (Tailwind ships static CSS), so no user input ever reaches it.
NO FORWARD FIX EXISTS. The advisory covers braces <=3.0.3 and 3.0.3 is the
latest release (checked 2026-10-23); micromatch 4.0.8, its latest, still
requires braces ^3.0.3, so an npm override cannot help. npm's remediation
is tailwindcss 4, a semver-major migration of the whole design system
(config, PostCSS setup, tailwindcss-animate and renamed utilities), which
is a project of its own, not a dependency bump.
ACTION ON EXPIRY: check for a patched braces (or a micromatch and chokidar
that drop it) and update if one exists; otherwise plan the Tailwind 4
migration. Delete this entry as soon as braces leaves the dependency tree.
If anything ever passes user-supplied globs or patterns to these packages,
delete this entry immediately: the argument above no longer holds.
